plan_title: Monitoring, Reporting, and Verification Plan, Red Hills AGI #1 and Red Hills AGI #3, Targa Northern Delaware, LLC (TND)
ama_definition: Set equal to the MMA: it covers the modeled plume at end of injection (2054) and five years later (2059), plus a half-mile buffer (p40).
mma_definition: The stabilized modeled acid gas plume at 2059 plus a half-mile buffer (p40).
leakage_pathways_rated_significant: Surface equipment (injection wells, the line to them, flanges, relief valves) is the most likely pathway; lateral migration along channel sands is rated possible; existing and groundwater wells possible-to-improbable with minimal magnitude; seal, faults and seismicity improbable per NRAP modeling (p41-46).
baseline_summary: DCS operating data and H2S Contingency Plan monitoring, plus purpose-built baselines: 12 months of monthly groundwater and soil CO2 flux sampling, and historical seismic records (p53-55). Plan says baseline monitoring has been under way for several years (p59).
reporting_summary: Annual Subpart RR reporting through GHG reports and records retention; pipeline leaks reported to NMOCD; NMBGMR seismic analysis and maps to be made publicly available; a groundwater chemistry report to be prepared; TND to take over monitoring, recording and reporting of the New Mexico Tech network data. No commitment to publish other measurement data (p52-54, p61-62).

rows.detail: Orifice volumetric meters (AGA Report #3) on the receiving pipelines (M1, M2) and on the lines to each AGI well (M3, M6), with daily totalizers; acid gas concentration sampled biweekly at sample points.
rows.location: Plant inlet meters and injection lines to RH AGI #1 and #3
rows.evidence_quote: Daily CO2 injected is recorded by totalizers on the volumetric flow meters

rows.detail: Plant DCS continuously monitors injection rates, pressures and composition against high and low set points that alert engineering and operations; plant staffed 24/7.
rows.trigger_or_response: Parameter outside allowable window: investigation of leak threat; leak indicated: shut in well and quantify.
rows.evidence_quote: The DCS of the plant monitors injection rates, pressures, and composition on a continuous basis.

rows.detail: Downhole gauge in each AGI well reads pressure and temperature in the tubing-casing annulus; data recorded onsite and sent offsite for daily real-time review.
rows.trigger_or_response: Annulus and tubing gauges reading the same pressure indicates a leak; well shut in and leak quantified.
rows.evidence_quote: the second gauge monitors the annular space between the tubing and the long string casing

rows.detail: MITs under NMOCC Rule 26 and permit conditions, listed as a detection method for the AGI wells; plan gives no test interval.
rows.trigger_or_response: Failed MIT: well shut in, leak characterized and quantified.
rows.evidence_quote: Rule 26 also includes requirements for testing and monitoring of Class II injection wells to ensure they maintain mechanical integrity at all times.

rows.detail: One downhole gauge in each AGI well reads tubing (reservoir) pressure and temperature continuously; recorded by an onsite interrogator and sent offsite for analysis.
rows.evidence_quote: One gauge is designated to monitor the tubing ID (reservoir) pressure and temperature

rows.detail: Field personnel follow daily and weekly inspection protocols on surface equipment; routine O&M procedures provide frequent periodic inspection of the wells.
rows.location: Plant surface equipment and AGI wellheads
rows.trigger_or_response: Leak found: immediate response, isolate the leak point, quantify.
rows.evidence_quote: following daily and weekly inspection protocols which include reporting and responding to any detected leakage events

rows.detail: All plant personnel wear H2S monitors (alarm 10 ppm); handheld detectors with H2S, CO2, LEL and oxygen sensors are kept at strategic points for checks before maintenance.
rows.location: Worn by plant personnel and contractors; handhelds around plant
rows.trigger_or_response: Alarm: response under H2S Contingency Plan; any CO2 leak quantified.
rows.evidence_quote: All personnel working at the Plant wear personal H2S monitors.

rows.detail: Numerous fixed H2S detectors (Red Line RL-101) and LEL detectors around plant and AGI wells, wired to PLC and DCS, calibrated monthly; plan says in-field monitors detect H2S and CO2.
rows.location: Throughout plant and around RH AGI wells, including temporarily abandoned AGI #2
rows.trigger_or_response: 10 ppm: beacons and alarm; 90 ppm: plant evacuation; immediate response to characterize and quantify.
rows.evidence_quote: TND also maintains in-field gas monitors to detect H2S and CO2.

rows.detail: Soil CO2 flux by LI-COR LI-8100A chamber on fixed collars at 32 locations: monthly for 12 months, bimonthly for a year, then quarterly. Set up by New Mexico Tech under a DOE grant.
rows.location: 32 CO2 flux locations in the AMA (Figure 7-1)
rows.trigger_or_response: Detected leak: decide if surface equipment or subsurface source; flux methods used to quantify subsurface leaks.
rows.evidence_quote: Soil CO2 flux will be collected on a monthly basis for 12 months to establish the baseline

rows.detail: Groundwater wells sampled for TDS, pH, alkalinity, major ions, ORP, inorganic and organic carbon: monthly for 12 months, bimonthly for a year, then quarterly. Run by New Mexico Tech under a DOE grant.
rows.trigger_or_response: Samples outside expected variation: investigate whether leakage from the injection zone has occurred.
rows.evidence_quote: Water samples will be collected and analyzed on a monthly basis for 12 months to establish baseline data.

rows.detail: Fiber-optic distributed temperature sensing clamped to the tubing in each AGI well records the annulus temperature profile from about 6,159 ft to surface. Permanent sensing, not logging runs.
rows.trigger_or_response: Temperature profile anomalies flag possible tubing or casing leaks.
rows.evidence_quote: DTS is clamped to the tubing, and it monitors the temperature profiles of the annulus from 6,159 ft to surface.

rows.detail: Operator-installed Trillium Compact Horizon seismometer at the plant (required by NMOCC order), plus state NMTSO network within 10 miles analyzed by NMBGMR.
rows.location: Plant site station plus NMTSO stations within 10 miles
rows.trigger_or_response: Leak signals linked to a seismic event: assess whether CO2 came from AGI wells and quantify.
rows.evidence_quote: TND has Installed a model TCH120-1 Trillium Compact Horizon Seismometer and a model CTR4-3S Centaur Digital Recorder

rows.detail: Licensed 3D seismic used in site characterization and the geologic model; no repeat seismic.
rows.evidence_quote: The static model is constructed with well tops and licensed 3D seismic data

rows.detail: The New Mexico Tech/DOE monitoring network scope includes periodic atmospheric sampling over 10-15 square miles around the injection wells; instruments and frequency not stated.
rows.location: 10-15 square miles around the injection wells
rows.evidence_quote: These activities include periodic well (groundwater and gas) and atmospheric sampling from an area of 10 – 15 square miles around the injection wells.

rows.detail: Subpart W (Table W-1A factors) for equipment between injection meter and wellhead; major leaks quantified from duration, pressure, temperature, composition and leak size; pipeline leak procedure under NMAC 19.15.28 to be adapted.
rows.trigger_or_response: Leak identified: isolate location, then quantify.
rows.evidence_quote: quantification of emissions of CO2 from surface equipment will be assessed by employing the methods detailed in Subpart W

rows.detail: Inline inspections listed as a surface-equipment detection method in Table 6-1; no further detail.
Plume model calibrated to RH AGI #1 injection history; to be reevaluated periodically as the state requires, and reassessed if monitoring shows the plume beyond the modeled area.
rows.trigger_or_response: Plume beyond modeled area: reassess modeling and submit revised MRV plan.
rows.evidence_quote: will be reevaluated periodically as required by the State permitting agency

rows.detail: More frequent monitoring and NMOCD H2S precautions when any new well is drilled through the injection zones within the MMA, by TND or other operators.
rows.location: New wells penetrating the injection zones
rows.evidence_quote: including more frequent monitoring during drilling operations

notes: PDF page 1 is a cover notice only; figure pages (detector map p28, monitoring network map p56) and appendix records (p87-92) are image-only. Groundwater, soil flux and atmospheric work are run by New Mexico Tech under a DOE grant, with TND to take over. DTS coded as cased_hole_logging though it is permanent fiber. MIT interval not stated. No production at site (p58), so production_monitoring is not_found. Monitoring covers injection plus a 5-year post-injection period (p47). Atmospheric sampling is coded committed (periodic, unspecified) to match Wildcat, whose plan uses the same language (p52-53), although no instruments, locations or frequency are given and the Figure 7-1 network map shows none.
